label: prop:area-formula
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:area-formula} Consider $V$ as in \Cref{thr:main}. Define $A(t) = |\{V \leq t\}|$, then $A\in C^0([0,+\infty))\cap C^1((0,+\infty))$. For $ t \in (0,+\infty)$ we have
    \[A'(t) = \int_{V=t} \frac{1}{|\nabla V|} \, \text{d} \mathcal H^{d-1}.\]
Moreover, $A$ is strictly increasing on $[0,+\infty)$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $C_\infty > 0$ play the role of $C$ in \Cref{prop:flow}, then there exists $\delta >0$ and a $C^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ diffeomorphism, $\Psi_s$, for $|s|\leq \delta$ we have $\Psi_s(\{V\leq C_\infty\}) = \{V\leq C_\infty+s\}$. Choosing $s = C_m - C_\infty$ and denoting $\Psi_m \coloneq \Psi_{C_m - C_\infty}$ we obtain $\Psi_m(\{V \leq C_\infty\}) = \{V\leq C_m\}$. Moreover, for $m$ sufficiently large we have that $|C_m - C_\infty| < \delta$, since $C_m \to C_\infty$ by \Cref{lem:cm-convergence}. Thus, by \eqref{eq:flow-estimate}, estimate \eqref{eq:psi-m-estimate} holds. 

It remains to prove \eqref{eq:collar-identity}. Recall that $\chi=1$ on $\{C_\infty-\delta\leq V\leq C_\infty+\delta\}$ (see \Cref{app:geometric-results}). Since $C_m\to C_\infty$, for $m$ sufficiently large we have $|C_m-C_\infty|\leq\delta/3$. Let $s_m\coloneq C_m-C_\infty$ and fix $x\in\{C_\infty-\delta/3\leq V\leq C_\infty+\delta/3\}$. We claim that the trajectory $t\mapsto\Psi_{ts_m}(x)$ remains in the region where $\chi=1$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. Indeed, otherwise let $t_0$ be its first exit time from $\{C_\infty-\delta<V<C_\infty+\delta\}$. For every $t<t_0$ we have $\chi(\Psi_{ts_m}(x))=1$, and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pre-exit-identity}
\frac{\, \text{d}}{\, \text{d} t}V(\Psi_{ts_m}(x))=s_m\nabla V(\Psi_{ts_m}(x))\cdot b(\Psi_{ts_m}(x))=s_m.
\end{equation}
Hence $V(\Psi_{ts_m}(x))=V(x)+ts_m$ for every $t<t_0$, and consequently
\[
|V(\Psi_{ts_m}(x))-C_\infty|\leq |V(x)-C_\infty|+t|s_m|\leq\frac{2\delta}{3}<\delta,
\]
which contradicts the definition of $t_0$. Thus the trajectory remains entirely in the region where $\chi=1$, and integrating \eqref{eq:pre-exit-identity} on $[0,1]$ and recalling $s_m = C_m - C_\infty$ gives
\[
V(\Psi_m(x))=V(x)+C_m-C_\infty.
\]
Rearranging, we obtain
\[
C_m-V(\Psi_m(x))=C_\infty-V(x)
\]
for every $x\in\{C_\infty-\delta/3\leq V\leq C_\infty+\delta/3\}$.

body_md:
The set $\{V<C_\infty\}$ is a bounded connected domain with $C^2$ boundary. By elliptic regularity for the Neumann problem (see \cite[Theorem~B.2]{BS25}) and the Sobolev embedding for $q>d$, we obtain
\[
\|\nabla u_m\|_{L^\infty(\{V<C_\infty\})}
\lesssim \|\nabla u_m\|_{W^{1,q}(\{V<C_\infty\})}
\lesssim \|\tilde\rho_m-1\|_{L^q(\{V<C_\infty\})}.
\]
The implicit constants depend only on the domain and $q$, and are therefore independent of $m$.

body_md:
Let $C>0$, and let $b$, $\delta$ and $\Psi_s$ be as in the proof of \Cref{prop:flow}. Thus, we have $\Psi_s(\{V\leq C\}) = \{V\leq C+s\}$, hence $|\Psi_s(\{V\leq C\})| = A(C+s)$. By the change of variables we have \[A(C+s) = \int_{\{V\leq C\}} \operatorname{det} D \Psi_s(x) \, \text{d} x.\]By \eqref{eq:jacobian-formula}, for $|s| < \delta$
\[A(C+s) = \int_{\{V\leq C\}}\underbrace{\exp\left( \int_0^s (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_\tau(x)) \, \text{d} \tau\right)}_{g(x,s)} \, \text{d} x.\] Since the function $(x,s) \mapsto g(x,s)$ is continuous, $(x,s)\mapsto \partial_sg(x, s)$ is continuous and bounded on $\{V\leq C\} \times [-\delta, \delta]$, we may differentiate under the integral sign to obtain \[\frac{d}{ds} A(C+s) = \int_{V\leq C} (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_s(x))\exp\left( \int_0^s (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_\tau(x)) \, \text{d} \tau\right) \, \text{d} x.\] Now we show that $s \mapsto \frac{d}{ds} A(C+s)$ is continuous: Let $s_n \to s$, then by continuity we have \[
\begin{aligned}
&(\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_{s_n}(x))
\exp\left(
    \int_0^{s_n}
    (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_\tau(x))
    \, \text{d} \tau
\right)
\\
&\qquad \longrightarrow
(\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_s(x))
\exp\left(
    \int_0^s
    (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_\tau(x))
    \, \text{d} \tau
\right).
\end{aligned}
\] and \[\left | (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_{s_n}(x))\exp\left( \int_0^{s_n} (\nabla \cdot b)(\Psi_\tau(x)) \, \text{d} \tau\right) \right | \leq \Vert \nabla \cdot  b \Vert_\infty \exp(\Vert \nabla \cdot b \Vert_\infty  \delta)\]hence, continuity of $s\mapsto \frac{d}{ds} A(C+s)$ follows by dominated convergence. We thus obtain that $A$ is of class $C^1$ in a neighbourhood of $C$, and since $C>0$ was arbitrarily taken, we have $A\in C^1((0,+\infty))$.

We still must show that $A$ is continuous at $ 0$. From the assumptions on $V$ it follows that the unique minimizer of $V$ is $x=0$, thus $A(0) = |\{V\leq0\}| = 0$. Let $t_n$ be a decreasing sequence converging to zero, then \[\lim_{t_n \to 0} A(t_n) = \lim_{t_n \to 0} |\{V\leq t_n\}| = \left| \cap_{n} \{ V\leq t_n \} \right| = |\{V=0\}| = 0 = A(0).\]

By \eqref{eq:jacobian-derivative} we obtain \[\begin{aligned}
     A
'(C) &= \frac{d}{ds} A(C+s) \bigg \vert_{s=0} \\& = \int_{\{V\leq C\}} \frac{\, \text{d}}{\, \text{d} s} \operatorname{det} D\Psi_s(x) \bigg \vert_{s=0} \, \text{d} x \\&= \int_{\{V\leq C\}} \nabla \cdot b \,  \, \text{d} x,
\end{aligned} \] and using the divergence theorem, observering that the outward unit normal vector on the set $\{V=C\}$ is $\frac{\nabla V}{|\nabla V|}$, we have \[A'(C) = \int_{\{V=C\}} b \cdot \frac{\nabla V}{|\nabla V|} \, \text{d} \mathcal H^{d-1} = \int_{\{V = C\}} \frac{1}{|\nabla V|}\, \text{d} \mathcal H^{d-1}.\]


Finally, for every $t>0$ we have that $\{V=t\}\neq \emptyset$ and $\nabla V \neq 0$ on $\{V=t\}$, thus, \[A'(t) = \int_{\{V=t\}} \frac{1}{|\nabla V|} \, \text{d} \mathcal{H}^{d-1} > 0,\] which implies that $A$ is strictly increasing on $(0,+\infty)$. Since $A(0) = 0 < A(t)$ for every $t>0$, $A$ is actually strictly increasing on the larger set $[0,+\infty)$.
